hook: Matrimony match led to a fake trading app: *₹12.75 lakh* gone
hook_b: Matrimony match led to a fake trading app: *₹12.75 lakh* gone
tldr: A 32-year-old Nagole businessman was cheated after a matrimony-site contact steered him to a fake forex and gold trading platform.

beats.what: He sent over ₹12.75 lakh in 10 transactions on instructions from a 'support executive' on Telegram.
beats.why: Screenshots of supposed profits won his trust; withdrawals were then blocked.
beats.care: Malkajgiri cybercrime police booked a case under BNS cheating and IT Act sections.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The contact began on a matrimony website in Feb 2025 and moved to WhatsApp.

cards.q: Has an online match or stranger ever pitched you an investment?

qs: Why do fake platforms ask for 'taxes' before releasing money?

facts.t: The money went out in *10 separate transactions* over months.

viz.verdict: The extra demands would have pushed losses up by nearly half; he refused.

watch: Whether Malkajgiri cybercrime police trace the accounts behind the platform.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Businessman loses ₹12 lakh after woman he met on matrimony site lures him into fake forex, gold trading in Hyderabad

fact: A Nagole man lost *₹12.75 lakh* to a matrimony match's fake trading app
twist: To 'release' his money, the platform demanded another *₹6.15 lakh* in taxes and fees.
